name: Talarozole

lead: Talarozole (formerly R115866, planned name Rambazole) is an investigational drug that raises retinoic acid levels in tissue without supplying a retinoid. The payoff sought was clearer, smoother skin in acne and psoriasis.

It inhibits CYP26A1 and CYP26B1, the enzymes that clear all-trans-retinoic acid, so retinoid signalling rises. A small phase I study of topical talarozole in healthy volunteers found gene-expression changes consistent with increased retinoic acid signalling and little irritation. Development for skin use is reported as discontinued, and it has more recently drawn attention in osteoarthritis research.

paras: It was studied as a topical and oral treatment in clinical development. It is not marketed, so there is no routine around it.
A small volunteer study found low irritation with topical use. It is not approved anywhere and long-term data are lacking.

angle.text: Talarozole is an investigational retinoic-acid blocker developed for acne and psoriasis, raising retinoid signalling in skin for clearer, smoother results. Skin development was discontinued, and cosmetic use has not been studied.

lead: Talarozole (formerly R115866; planned trade name Rambazole) is an investigational retinoic acid metabolism blocking agent (RAMBA). It inhibits the CYP26 enzymes, mainly CYP26A1 and CYP26B1, that break down all-trans-retinoic acid, so it raises retinoic acid signaling without supplying a retinoid [1][2]. It was developed for acne, psoriasis and other keratinization disorders, and development for those skin uses is reported as discontinued [2].

Human data are early-phase. A small phase I study of topical talarozole on healthy volunteers found gene-expression changes consistent with increased retinoic acid signaling and little irritation [3]. More recently it has attracted attention in osteoarthritis research [4]. It is not approved anywhere and has no established cosmetic use.

paras: Talarozole is described as a potent inhibitor of CYP26A1 and CYP26B1, the enzymes that clear all-trans-retinoic acid [1]. Studies in cultured epidermis found that talarozole and liarozole altered retinoid-regulated genes and enzymes [5], and work on human keratinocytes implicated CYP26 in their retinoic acid metabolism [6]. Wikipedia reports it as roughly 750-fold more potent than liarozole and highly selective for CYP26A1 over CYP17A1 and aromatase [2].

In a randomized phase I trial, 16 healthy volunteers applied 0.35% or 0.07% talarozole gel or vehicle for 9 days. Biopsies showed dose-dependent increases in CRABP2, KRT4 and CYP26 mRNA, decreases in KRT2 and IL-1alpha, no increase in epidermal thickness and no overt inflammation, which the authors interpreted as increased retinoic acid stimulation with low irritancy [3].

Registered phase I and II trials covered oral talarozole in facial acne (n=16), plaque psoriasis (n=176 and n=19) and topical gel anti-inflammatory effects (n=12) [7][8][9][10]. Results are not summarized in the sources reviewed here. No trials in cosmetic skin ageing were found.

A 2022 study linked variants in ALDH1A2, a retinoic acid synthesis gene, to severe hand osteoarthritis. In cartilage and mouse models, talarozole reduced inflammatory gene activity, cartilage breakdown and osteophyte formation, leading the authors to propose RAMBAs as potential disease-modifying drugs for osteoarthritis [4]. Another group is studying selective CYP26B1 inhibitors for keratinization disorders [11].
